name: bluewater-08-ads-scoreboard
lines: On the first of the month, fifteen hundred dollars leaves Priya's bank account.
It goes to ads. It has gone to ads every month for a year.
Eighteen thousand dollars. And she cannot tell you one job it brought her.
If that sounds familiar, this one is for you.
Priya is invented. Her bank statement is not.
She runs a landscaping company. Eleven years. Two crews. She started with one mower and a borrowed truck.
A year ago a guy named Blake sold her on ads.
Every month Blake sends a report. It has very big numbers on it.
Forty eight thousand people saw your ad. Nine hundred people clicked.
The report is twelve pages long. It has charts. It has arrows pointing up.
It looks amazing. Priya feels good for about a minute.
Then she asks the only question that matters. How many of them called?
Blake does not know. Nobody is counting. And every month the money leaves anyway.
That night she spreads twelve months of reports across the kitchen table.
Impressions. Clicks. Reach. Not one line says jobs.
Eighteen thousand dollars in. And no way to know what came out.
Priya is not bad at business. She was just handed the wrong scoreboard.
So she builds her own.
It has three boxes. Money out. Calls in. Jobs won.
Here is how ads really work. An ad is a tap.
Turn it on, calls can come. Turn it off, they stop. That is all it is.
There are two kinds. Search ads show up when someone types what you do.
Social ads show up while someone is scrolling past.
One catches people who are looking. The other catches people who are not. Yet.
Neither one is magic. Both are just a way to buy a chance at a call.
So the only number that matters is this. What did one new customer cost you?
Take what you spent. Divide by the customers it brought. That is your number.
Then put that next to what a job pays you after costs.
If the job pays more than the customer cost, keep going. If it does not, stop and fix something.
Fix one. Count every call.
Ask every new caller one question. How did you find us?
Write the answer down. On paper, in your phone, anywhere.
Better still, give your ads their own phone number, so the calls count themselves.
Many business phone services can give you a second number for this.
After thirty days Priya has her first real number. Six calls. One job.
Fifteen hundred dollars for one customer. On a job that pays twenty four hundred.
After crew and materials, she lost money on it.
Fix two. Send the ad to one page about one thing.
Her ad said patio. It sent people to her home page. Lawns, hedges, snow, everything.
They came for a patio and had to hunt for it. So they left.
Now the ad says patio, and the page says patio.
Photos of real patios. A price range. A phone number at the top.
Put one review on that page. From a patio customer.
Take out the menu. Every extra link is a way to leave.
One ad. One page. One thing to do. Call.
Fix three. Answer fast.
A person who clicks an ad is often calling three companies. The first one to pick up has the best shot.
Priya's calls were going to voicemail while she was on a mower.
Now they ring the office first. And a missed call gets a call back within five minutes.
And here is what Blake never told her. People who click an ad still look you up.
If your reviews are thin and your photos are old, the ad just sends them to someone else.
Ads pour the water. Reviews and real photos are the bucket.
Three mistakes eat ad budgets.
Boosting a post with no goal. It gets likes. Likes do not dig patios.
Changing everything after three days. Ads need a few weeks to settle.
And paying for clicks from two towns over. Set your area to where your crews really go.
Then she runs a fair test. Thirty more days. Same budget.
Fifteen calls. Five jobs.
Fifteen hundred dollars divided by five. Three hundred dollars a customer.
On a twenty four hundred dollar job, that is a tap worth leaving on.
Same money. Five times the work.
She did not spend one dollar more. She just started counting.
Blake sends his report anyway. Fifty one thousand impressions.
Priya writes back with one line. How many called?
She never hears from Blake again.
The first of the next month. Fifteen hundred dollars leaves her account.
This time she knows exactly where it is going.
The patio page. The tracked number. The office phone that always gets answered.
And by the end of the month, she knows what it brought back. Twelve thousand dollars of work.
Nobody can promise you ads will work. Sometimes they do not.
If the number is bad after a fair test, turn the tap off and fix the page.
Start with a budget you can afford to lose. This is a test, not a bet.
But never pay for ads you cannot count.
Priya did not need a bigger budget. She needed a scoreboard.
So do this tonight. Find your last ad bill.
Then ask Priya's question. How many called? How many became jobs?
If you do not know, that is your first fix.
Count the calls. One page for one thing. Answer fast.
That is all of it. If you want a hand, we are Bluewater Co.
